key_insight: For fermionic impurity models with fixed impurity size, quantum algorithms prepare low-temperature thermal states with polynomial inverse-temperature cost and polylogarithmic precision cost.
engineering_relevance: These algorithms could support quantum simulations of strongly correlated materials through impurity problems central to dynamical mean field theory.
method: Use quantum Gibbs samplers with global jump operators to avoid the usual exponential inverse-temperature overhead.
Prepare thermal states and their purifications in time poly(n, β, log(1/δ)).
Use purification to estimate static and dynamical properties with Heisenberg scaling in precision.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity guarantees, including efficient ground-state preparation for inverse-polynomial spectral gaps, rather than numerical or hardware benchmarks.
watch_item: The guarantees assume fixed impurity size; practical resource costs and implementation of global jump operators remain important considerations.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
